title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is a commutative ring, M an A-module, and B = Sym*(M) ⊗ Λ*(M), graded by the Λ-degree. The page is the first of a short catalogue of four 'complexes d'algèbre différentielle'. The next page treats the divided-power analogues on Γ*(M) ⊗ Λ*(M). The catalogue prepares the 'complexe de De Rham à puissances divisées' that is the subject of the 1976 IHÉS lecture.

(1) De Rham. There is a unique A-linear antiderivation d of the graded algebra B with these properties: it vanishes on Λ^1 M, and on Sym^1 M it is the canonical isomorphism Sym^1 M → Λ^1 M.
- Then d^2 = 0, d maps Sym^p⊗Λ^q to Sym^{p-1}⊗Λ^{q+1}, and d is Λ*M-linear.
- This is the algebraic de Rham complex Ω^•_{Sym(M)/A} of the 'vector bundle' V(M) = Spec Sym(M) over A (EGA notation).
- Claim: if A is a Q-algebra and M is flat, then H^i = 0 for i ≠ 0 and H^0 = A = Sym^0⊗Λ^0. This is the algebraic Poincaré lemma.
- In characteristic p the cohomology is larger, governed by the Cartier operation. Grothendieck only alludes to this ('histoire des opérations de Cartier ...').

(2) Koszul. There is a unique antiderivation δ of B with these properties: it vanishes on Sym^1 M (hence is Sym(M)-linear), and on Λ^1 M it is the canonical isomorphism Λ^1 M → Sym^1 M.
- Then δ^2 = 0 and δ maps Sym^p⊗Λ^q to Sym^{p+1}⊗Λ^{q-1}; it has bidegree (+1,-1), i.e. degree -1 in the Λ-grading.
- Claim: for M flat (e.g. free), with no characteristic hypothesis, the homology is A in degree 0 and zero otherwise.
- In other words, Sym(M)⊗Λ(M) is the Koszul resolution of A = Sym(M)/M·Sym(M) as a Sym(M)-module. For free M this is the usual Koszul complex. The flat case follows by Lazard's theorem and passage to filtered colimits.

Underlying both results is the identity dδ + δd = (p+q)·id on Sym^p⊗Λ^q, the Euler/homotopy formula. In characteristic 0 it gives the contraction of both complexes in positive total degree.

The next page repeats the pattern for Γ*(M)⊗Λ*(M):
- (3) PD de Rham, with d(x^[i]) = x^[i-1]dx, acyclic for M flat in every characteristic.
- (4) PD Koszul, acyclic in characteristic 0, with a Cartier-type story expected in characteristic p.

The overall picture is a 2×2 table: {Sym, Γ} × {de Rham, Koszul}. Under Sym ↔ Γ the acyclicity hypotheses swap. Ordinary de Rham and PD Koszul need characteristic 0 (or have Cartier phenomena in characteristic p). Ordinary Koszul and PD de Rham are acyclic for flat M in any characteristic. The PD de Rham case is the PD Poincaré lemma underlying crystalline cohomology.
errors: Hypotheses stronger than needed: in characteristic 0 the identity dδ+δd = (p+q)·id contracts both the de Rham and the Koszul complex in positive total degree for ANY A-module M. The flatness assumption in (1) is therefore superfluous over a Q-algebra; it is only needed for (2) in arbitrary characteristic.
Minor slip in (2): the homology is written H_q^{Kos} but the cases are indexed by i.
Nothing is actually stated in characteristic p for the de Rham case; it is left as 'histoire des opérations de Cartier ...'. No errors in the stated claims.

ideas.what: Algebraic de Rham complex of Sym(M), i.e. of the vector bundle V(M), described as the unique antiderivation on Sym⊗Λ extending Sym^1 ≅ Λ^1; acyclic in characteristic 0 (algebraic Poincaré lemma)
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic Poincaré lemma / de Rham complex of a polynomial algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (folklore); in this generality e.g. Illusie, Complexe cotangent et déformations; Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) uses the algebraic de Rham complex, but not this formulation

ideas.what: Koszul complex Sym(M)⊗Λ(M) as a resolution of A for flat M in any characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Koszul, Cartan–Eilenberg; flat case via Lazard; Illusie, Complexe cotangent I, Ch. I §4
ideas.where_published: Koszul complexes appear in EGA III/IV and SGA 6 (written with Berthelot and Illusie), not in this form

ideas.what: The 2×2 table {Sym, Γ}×{de Rham, Koszul}, in which characteristic hypotheses swap under Sym ↔ Γ, with Cartier operations expected in characteristic p
ideas.modern_name: Koszul duality between Sym and Γ; PD Poincaré lemma; Cartier isomorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (crystalline cohomology, 1974); Illusie (Complexe cotangent I, 1971, Ch. I 4.3; de Rham–Witt, 1979)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard background material: de Rham and Koszul complexes of a symmetric algebra and their acyclicity, set up as preparation for the PD de Rham complex. It is well covered by Illusie and Berthelot. The only mild interest is the systematic four-way presentation and the anticipated Cartier story for the characteristic-0-only cases.
transcription_corrections: 'dans le complexe de De Rham du fibré vectoriel V(M)' should read 'donc le complexe de De Rham du fibré vectoriel V(M) sur A'.
The parenthetical under the De Rham cohomology formula reads approximately '(i.e. A est une Q-alg.), M plat', restating the characteristic-0 hypothesis. It is not '(A est une F_p-alg., M plat)'.
The marginal word 'inutile' refers to the struck-out passage on H*(Sym*(M)⊗Λ*M), with a diagonal stroke linking them.
Opening line: 'A anneau commutatif, M A-module. On considère Sym*(M)⊗Λ*M et Γ*(M)⊗Λ*M comme A-alg. graduées par degré de Λ*M' — consistent with the image.
